title: Cold-water drowning - hypothermic arrest
objectives: Start decision: < 6 C water, submerged < 90 min -> full resuscitation; stiffness/fixed pupils are not death (2.13/4.2)
Ventilation first: airway + breaths before compressions; no draining water
Hypothermia limits: 60-s pulse check, gentle handling, 1 shock max, no epi while presumed < 30 C (MD)
No TOR until rewarmed to 32 C; transport with CPR to CPB/ECMO center (UVMMC) via MD
Pre-arrival prep: heated unit, warm fluids, timeline (immersion vs submersion)
resources: AED/monitor, BVM, OPA, suction, SGA, IV/IO, warm NS (40-42 C), epi 0.1 mg/mL, heat packs, blankets, Stokes basket, capno, metronome. Shelburne FD ice team. UVMMC (cardiac surgery/CPB) ~18 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue and Shelburne Fire, respond to Shelburne Pond, Pond Rd fishing access, for an adult male through the ice. Caller is his wife. Fire ice rescue en route. Time out 1556.

scene.location: Shelburne Pond fishing access, dusk, 28 F, wind. Thin early ice. 80 m steep path from shore to ambulance.
scene.setup: Crew stages on shore while FD ice team works. Pt slips under ~1612; FD hands him over on a tarp at T+0 (~1621). Manikin wet (spray bottle).
scene.moulage: Wet jacket w/ ice chips, blue-gray lips, froth at mouth (shaving cream), vomit 1-2 min into BVM.
scene.roles: Wife (frantic); FD ice rescuers (1 joins CPR); evaluator calls AED + pulse.

patient.name: Mark Gagnon
patient.cc: Through the ice, pulled from water
patient.on_arrival: Limp, gray, soaked, ice on clothes. Not breathing. Jaw and limbs stiff.

SAMPLE: Wife: "He went out after the dog, the ice broke"
Through ice ~1550, holding edge + talking; under ~1612; out ~1621

primary: Froth at mouth; vomit after breaths -> suction. No draining water
Apneic -> a few BVM breaths w/ O2 first
No pulse on 60-s check -> CPR + AED
Soaked, ice on clothes -> cut off, dry, wrap, heat packs
Hypothermic arrest after immersion -> **resuscitate, transport with CPR**
secondary: Stiff jaw/limbs + fixed pupils = **cold, not death** (2.13)
No visible injury; no collar needed (4.2)
Tympanic 'LO' - not a core temp (4.2 Pearl)
vitals_note: Arrest stages are 2-min cycles from contact on shore. Pulse 0 = CPR. Temp LO = below thermometer range.

vitals.other: **VF persists** - AED advises shock again. Core presumed < 30 C

vitals.trigger: IF compressions w/o breaths, no chest rise, or vomit not suctioned
vitals.other: No chest rise, gurgling. Fix airway -> back to Stage B values
VF continues. Hypothermic - TOR rule not applicable (8.17)

vitals.trigger: Examiner inject en route ~T+26 (analysis: no shock)
vitals.other: Faint carotid on 60-s check. Stop CPR; gentle; warm NS

vitals.trigger: IF rough handling/fast move after Stage E
vitals.other: **VF** - pulse lost. Resume CPR; MD before any further shock

flow.give: Man holding ice edge ~40 yd out; FD team going out. He slips under ~1612. Wife: "He was talking to me, then he went under!"
expected: Unit heated to 24 C; heat packs, blankets, warm NS (40-42 C) ready (2.13)
Timeline: time in water, time under, water temp (4.2)
Intercept requested; MD/UVMMC early re: CPB/ECMO destination

flow.give: Pt handed over. Stage **A**. FF: "He's stiff and his pupils are blown - he's gone, right?"

branches.if: Crew withholds: stiff, fixed pupils, 'under too long'
branches.then: critical (evaluator discretion) - not death signs in hypothermia; < 6 C + < 90 min -> resuscitate (2.13/4.2)

branches.if: Compressions first, no breaths / no chest rise

expected.text: Gentle, horizontal; pulse/breathing check up to 60 s (2.13)
Airway + a few BVM breaths w/ O2 before compressions (4.2)

expected: CPR + AED; no collar w/o trauma; no draining water

flow.give: Analysis 1 VF -> shock. Stage **B**: AED advises shock again each analysis.

branches.then: debrief 2.13: 1 shock if < 30 C, warm before more
expect suction, turn as a unit, keep ventilating; ignored -> Stage **C**

expected: 1 shock max, then CPR only - no further shocks (2.13)

expected.text: Wet clothes off, dry, heat packs neck/axilla/groin, wrap

expected: IV/IO w/o pausing CPR; warm NS 500 mL (2.13)

flow.give: Steep 80 m path. If MD asked about epi: "Hold epi while he's this cold."

branches.if: Epi given q other cycle per routine 3.2A
branches.then: debrief 2.13: no vasoactive drugs < 30 C; MD first

expected: Epi withheld: core presumed < 30 C, no core temp -> MD (2.13)
Flat in Stokes; CPR continuous, or 5 on/5 off only if needed to evacuate (2.13)

flow.give: En route UVMMC. Stage **D** at T+20. Partner: "20 minutes, EtCO2 7 - do we call it?"

branches.if: Crew asks MD for TOR at 20 min
branches.then: critical (evaluator discretion) - no TOR until rewarmed to 32 C (8.17/2.13); low EtCO2 not predictive (4.2)

expected: CPR continued to UVMMC; compressor swaps q2 min, belted

flow.give: Inject below, else arrive UVMMC with CPR running.

branches.if: Slow organized rhythm, faint pulse en route
branches.then: Stage **E**; expect 60-s check, stop CPR, gentle
Stage **F** - VF; CPR, MD re: shocks

expected: HR 28 w/ pulse = no CPR; very gentle handling (2.13 Pearl)
SGA vent ~5/min (half rate, 2.13); warm NS if SBP < 90
Report: time in water/under, water temp, 1 shock, no epi

critical: Resuscitation withheld for stiffness/fixed pupils/'too long' (< 6 C water, < 90 min) (4.2/2.13)
No ventilation-first approach / no BVM w/ O2 (4.2)
Pulse check rushed (< 60 s) or rough handling (2.13)
Repeated shocks after 1st shock with core presumed < 30 C (2.13)
Epi given with core presumed < 30 C, no MD contact (2.13)
No active warming / wet clothes left on (2.13)
TOR requested or CPR stopped before rewarming (8.17)
CPB/ECMO destination not discussed with MD/UVMMC (2.13)
differentials: ~20 min clinging (cooled first), 2 C water, VF, temp LO
Cooled before going under - better prognosis
No dive or fall from height; no injury seen
debrief: Immersion vs submersion: why does it matter that he held on for 20 min first?
Why breaths before compressions here, and why not drain the water?
What changes for shocks and epi in hypothermic arrest? Who decides?
Why no TOR at 20 min, and what does a low EtCO2 mean in a cold patient?
Why does UVMMC (bypass/ECMO) matter, and why not wait for air medical?

crew_card.dispatch: Shelburne Pond, Pond Rd fishing access, Shelburne. Adult male through the ice. Caller: wife. Shelburne Fire ice rescue en route.
crew_card.on_arrival: Dusk, 28 F, wind. A man in the water ~40 yd out, arms on the ice edge, barely moving. Wife screaming on shore, wet dog beside her. Fire ice team heading out on the ice.

actor_card.Wife: "He went after the dog. He was holding on and talking to me - then he went under!" Gives times if asked calmly. Wants to ride.
actor_card.FD rescuer: At hand-over: "He's stiff and his pupils are blown - he's gone, right?" Does CPR if assigned.
actor_card.Partner (T+20): "20 minutes, EtCO2 7 - do we call it?"
actor_card.Medical Direction: If asked about epi: "Hold epi while he's this cold." Destination: UVMMC, notify for bypass/ECMO.
actor_card.Evaluator: Analysis 1: VF, shock advised. VF continues, AED keeps advising. No pulse unless you inject Stage E.

show_cards.caption: NO SHOCK ADVISED

show_cards.title: FIRE ICE TEAM
show_cards.body:
In water ~20 min holding the ice.
Went under ~1612.
Out of water ~1621.
Water ~36 F.
show_cards.cue: Hand over at shore if crew asks for times

learn_more.topic: hypothermic cardiac arrest after cold-water drowning
learn_more.focus: ventilation first, shock and epinephrine limits, gentle handling, no early termination, ECMO destination
